grades.name: Situation Snapshot
grades.description: Capture the immediate situation and the result you need.
grades.instruction: State the immediate situation and the result you need in two or three sentences.

grades.name: Working Brief
grades.description: Add the goal, available inputs, and practical boundaries.
grades.instruction: Describe the goal, the inputs available to work from, and the practical boundaries in play.

grades.name: Decision Context
grades.description: Explain the decision, its stakeholders, and what has been tried.
grades.instruction: Lay out the stakeholders, the decision being made, the constraints that bind it, and what has already been tried or ruled out.

grades.name: Complete Operating Picture
grades.description: Supply the full background needed to act without guessing.
grades.instruction: Supply the full operating picture — background, dependencies, prior decisions and their reasons, and the downstream effects a change would touch — so the work can proceed without guessing.

goals: State what is happening and what result is needed.
Give the model the inputs it may use.
Name the boundaries that shape a useful answer.

grades.name: Given As True
grades.description: Treat the supplied information as the working truth.
grades.instruction: Treat the supplied information as the working truth; do not spend effort second-guessing it.

grades.name: Source Support
grades.description: Ground load-bearing claims in credible references.
grades.instruction: Ground load-bearing claims in a credible reference, and say when you are relying on general knowledge instead.

grades.name: Corroborated Sources
grades.description: Cross-check the claims the conclusion depends on.
grades.instruction: Corroborate every claim the conclusion depends on across at least two independent, credible sources, and surface any disagreement between them.

grades.name: Audit Trail
grades.description: Make evidence, conflicts, and confidence fully traceable.
grades.instruction: Attach evidence to every material claim, note where sources conflict and which you weighted, and mark each key conclusion with your confidence and the reason for it.

goals: Show which claims need support.
Use sources strong enough for the decision.
Make uncertainty and disagreement visible.

grades.name: Basic Limits
grades.description: Respect the stated exclusions and say when they bind.
grades.instruction: Respect the stated exclusions; if a requirement collides with one, say so rather than quietly working around it.

grades.name: Operating Limits
grades.description: Work inside time, tool, budget, and scope limits.
grades.instruction: Work inside the stated time, tool, budget, and scope limits, and call out any recommendation that presses against one.

grades.name: Constraint Map
grades.description: Separate hard constraints from negotiable preferences.
grades.instruction: Separate hard constraints from negotiable preferences, honor the hard ones absolutely, and say which preferences you traded away and why.

grades.name: Boundary Conditions
grades.description: Treat dependencies, exceptions, and failure states explicitly.
grades.instruction: Treat dependencies, exceptions, and failure conditions as first-class constraints: state what breaks each recommendation and where its limits sit.

goals: Separate hard limits from preferences.
Account for time, budget, tools, and exclusions.
Prevent recommendations that cannot be used.

grades.name: Working Assumptions
grades.description: Say what is being assumed instead of building on it silently.
grades.instruction: When you must assume something to proceed, say so in one line rather than silently building on it.

grades.name: Assumption Check
grades.description: Flag the assumptions that would change the answer.
grades.instruction: List the assumptions that would change the answer if wrong, and mark the one that worries you most.

grades.name: Assumption Register
grades.description: Track each assumption, its basis, and its consequence.
grades.instruction: Keep a short register of material assumptions — each with its basis and the consequence if it fails — and refer back to it in the conclusion.

grades.name: Uncertainty Model
grades.description: Rank the unknowns and show how each shifts the answer.
grades.instruction: Model the uncertainty explicitly: rank the material unknowns by impact, show how each would shift the recommendation, and name what evidence would settle them.

goals: Expose assumptions instead of hiding them.
Flag assumptions that could change the result.
Connect uncertainty to the final recommendation.

grades.name: Done Means
grades.description: Name what success looks like and check against it.
grades.instruction: State, in one line, what a successful result looks like — and check the answer against it before finishing.

grades.name: Success Check
grades.description: Define a practical acceptance test and pass it.
grades.instruction: Define a practical acceptance test for the result and show that the answer passes it.

grades.name: Success Criteria
grades.description: Work against explicit success and failure conditions.
grades.instruction: Work against explicit success criteria and explicit failure conditions; if any criterion cannot be met, say which and why.

grades.name: Evaluation Framework
grades.description: Define measures and thresholds, then evaluate against them.
grades.instruction: Define measures, thresholds, and validation steps up front, and evaluate the final result against each one before presenting it.

goals: Define what a finished result must accomplish.
Give the model a practical acceptance test.
Name outcomes that would count as failure.

grades.name: No-Go List
grades.description: Respect the stated no-go items.
grades.instruction: Respect the stated no-go items; do not include or suggest them.

grades.name: Scope Fence
grades.description: Keep an explicit line between in and out of scope.
grades.instruction: Keep an explicit line between in-scope and out-of-scope; if useful ideas fall outside it, park them in one line instead of pursuing them.

grades.name: Anti-Goals
grades.description: Treat what this must not become as binding.
grades.instruction: Treat the anti-goals as binding: check the draft against them before finishing, and cut anything that drifts toward what this work must not become.

grades.name: Drift Alarm
grades.description: Actively police scope and flag any pull outside it.
grades.instruction: Police scope actively: if the task, the evidence, or your own reasoning pulls toward an excluded area, stop, flag the pull explicitly, and continue only inside the fence.

goals: Make out-of-scope explicit, not implied.
Stop good ideas from dragging the work off course.
Catch scope drift before it costs anything.

grades.name: Guided Review
grades.description: Review the material where the user points.
grades.instruction: Review the supplied material and report what it contains, following the user's pointers about where to look.

grades.name: Checklist Inspection
grades.description: Inspect against the stated questions and criteria.
grades.instruction: Inspect the inputs against the stated questions and criteria, and answer each one directly.

grades.name: Independent Inspection
grades.description: Decide what needs inspecting and report the gaps.
grades.instruction: Decide for yourself what needs inspecting, examine it, and report the material gaps, conflicts, and surprises you find.

grades.name: Full Audit
grades.description: Run a complete audit before acting.
grades.instruction: Plan and run a complete audit before acting: cover every relevant input, log the gaps and conflicts, and give a short verdict on whether the material is fit for the task.

goals: Review the available material before acting.
Find missing inputs, conflicts, and weak spots.
Use the inspection to guide the next step.

grades.name: Pattern Read
grades.description: Find the clearest patterns and what they suggest.
grades.instruction: Identify the clearest patterns in the material and explain plainly what they suggest.

grades.name: Rival Explanations
grades.description: Test the main pattern against a rival explanation.
grades.instruction: For the main pattern you find, test at least one rival explanation and say why you kept or rejected it.

grades.name: Critical Analysis
grades.description: Challenge assumptions, causes, and inferences.
grades.instruction: Pressure-test the reasoning: challenge the key assumptions, probe the causal claims, and separate what the evidence shows from what is being inferred.

grades.name: Adversarial Analysis
grades.description: Hunt for disconfirming evidence and failure modes.
grades.instruction: Actively try to break the conclusion — hunt for disconfirming evidence, hidden assumptions, and failure modes — and report what survived and what did not.

goals: Identify patterns, causes, and important differences.
Test the explanation against alternatives.
Separate evidence from assumption.

grades.name: Options on the Table
grades.description: Lay out the options and their core differences.
grades.instruction: Lay out the supplied options side by side and explain their core differences.

grades.name: Framed Comparison
grades.description: Compare against the stated criteria and constraints.
grades.instruction: Compare the options against the stated criteria and constraints, showing where each wins and loses.

grades.name: Weighted Comparison
grades.description: Choose and weight the criteria that matter here.
grades.instruction: Choose the comparison criteria yourself, weight them by what matters most here, and show the tradeoffs that actually change the decision.

grades.name: Decision Matrix
grades.description: Full matrix with scores, rationale, and a verdict.
grades.instruction: Build the full decision matrix — criteria, weights, scores, and rationale — and state which option wins, under what conditions the ranking flips, and what you excluded.

goals: Set clear criteria before judging options.
Show the tradeoffs that change the decision.
Make the preferred option easy to defend.

grades.name: Draft Together
grades.description: Rough first pass; surface the decisions needing direction.
grades.instruction: Produce a first rough pass quickly, and surface the decisions you need direction on before going further.

grades.name: Build to Plan
grades.description: Build faithfully from the supplied plan and constraints.
grades.instruction: Build the artifact from the supplied plan and constraints, following them faithfully and noting where they were ambiguous.

grades.name: Independent Build
grades.description: Make the silent decisions and deliver complete work.
grades.instruction: Make the implementation decisions yourself where the brief is silent — recording each one in a line — and deliver the complete artifact.

grades.name: End-to-End Delivery
grades.description: Plan, build, verify, and hand over the finished result.
grades.instruction: Own the delivery end to end: plan it, build it, verify it against the success criteria, and hand over the finished result with a note on what you checked.

goals: Turn the brief into a complete artifact.
Make reasonable choices where the brief is silent.
Check the work before presenting it.

grades.name: Directions
grades.description: Offer promising directions and when each fits.
grades.instruction: Offer two or three promising directions and say when each one fits best.

grades.name: Practical Pick
grades.description: Pick what fits the constraints, with the deciding reason.
grades.instruction: Recommend the option that best fits the stated constraints, and give the one reason that decides it.

grades.name: Backed Recommendation
grades.description: Commit, justify against the runner-up, and name the risk.
grades.instruction: Commit to one recommendation, justify it against the strongest alternative, and name the main risk of following it.

grades.name: Full Conviction
grades.description: Make the call as if you owned the outcome.
grades.instruction: Make the call as if you owned the outcome: one recommendation, the evidence that supports it, the conditions that would reverse it, and the first step to act on it.

goals: Choose a direction instead of only listing options.
Tie the choice to the stated constraints.
Justify the choice against the alternatives.

grades.name: Sanity Pass
grades.description: Quick pass for obvious errors and contradictions.
grades.instruction: Give the result a quick sanity pass for obvious errors, omissions, and contradictions.

grades.name: Criteria Check
grades.description: Verify each acceptance criterion, pass or fail.
grades.instruction: Verify the result against each stated acceptance criterion and report pass or fail per item.

grades.name: Stress Test
grades.description: Push on edge cases and likely failure modes.
grades.instruction: Stress-test the result against edge cases, awkward inputs, and the most likely failure modes; fix what breaks or say why it stands.

grades.name: Red Team
grades.description: Attack the result like a hostile reviewer.
grades.instruction: Attack the result as a hostile reviewer would — strongest counter-arguments, nastiest inputs, worst-case readings — and do not call it finished until the serious findings are resolved.

goals: Check the result against explicit criteria.
Look for omissions, edge cases, and failure modes.
Resolve serious weaknesses before calling it done.

grades.name: Key Points Pull
grades.description: Condense the material into its main points.
grades.instruction: Condense the supplied material into its main points without adding interpretation.

grades.name: Faithful Summary
grades.description: Summarize faithfully; flag what needs judgment.
grades.instruction: Summarize the material faithfully and flag the points that need the user's own judgment.

grades.name: Decision Summary
grades.description: Lead with what the reader needs; compress the rest.
grades.instruction: Decide what the reader actually needs from this material, lead with it, and compress everything else hard.

grades.name: Executive Distillation
grades.description: Bottom line first, then only what drives it.
grades.instruction: Distill the material to its decision-critical core: the bottom line first, the two or three facts that drive it, and nothing that does not change a decision.

goals: Capture the source's most important points.
Condense faithfully without distorting meaning.
Match the detail to what the reader needs.

grades.name: Supplied Sources
grades.description: Work from the given sources; list what is missing.
grades.instruction: Work strictly from the supplied sources and list what is missing to answer fully.

grades.name: Targeted Lookup
grades.description: Fill the specific gaps and cite where facts came from.
grades.instruction: Fill the specific gaps the task exposes, and cite where each found fact came from.

grades.name: Open Research
grades.description: Scope the investigation and weigh what you find.
grades.instruction: Scope the investigation yourself: decide what needs finding, gather it, and weigh the credibility of what you found.

grades.name: Deep Investigation
grades.description: Corroborate key claims and state confidence with reasons.
grades.instruction: Run the investigation to ground: corroborate the load-bearing claims, chase the disagreements to their source, and state confidence with reasons for each key finding.

goals: Find the information the task actually needs.
Weigh sources by credibility and relevance.
Separate what is known from what is assumed.

grades.name: Rough Outline
grades.description: Sketch the main steps in a sensible order.
grades.instruction: Sketch the main steps in a sensible order so the shape of the work is visible.

grades.name: Sequenced Plan
grades.description: Order the steps, mark dependencies, flag the risk.
grades.instruction: Sequence the steps, mark the dependencies between them, and flag the riskiest one.

grades.name: Delivery Plan
grades.description: Phase the work with milestones and verification.
grades.instruction: Phase the work into milestones with owners, dependencies, and a verification step per phase.

grades.name: Executable Program
grades.description: A plan someone could run without you.
grades.instruction: Produce a plan someone could run without you: phases, owners, dependencies, entry and exit criteria per phase, and the contingency for the most likely slip.

goals: Break the goal into ordered, doable steps.
Surface dependencies and the right sequence.
Make the plan something a team can execute.

grades.name: Quick Options
grades.description: A handful of distinct starting ideas.
grades.instruction: Offer a handful of distinct starting ideas, each in a line or two.

grades.name: Divergent Set
grades.description: A genuinely diverse set — vary the approach.
grades.instruction: Generate a genuinely diverse set of options — vary the approach, not the wording — and name what makes each one different.

grades.name: Explore and Converge
grades.description: Go wide, then pick the strongest and say why.
grades.instruction: Explore widely first, including at least one unconventional option, then converge: pick the two or three strongest and say what earned them the cut.

grades.name: Creative Sweep
grades.description: Sweep safe bets to wildcards, then rank and test.
grades.instruction: Sweep the option space deliberately — safe bets, adjacent moves, and wildcards — then rank the strongest candidates and state what would prove each one out.

goals: Generate genuinely different options, not variations.
Explore before converging.
Say what would prove the strongest ideas out.

grades.name: Direct Answer
grades.description: Explain the thing asked, no more.
grades.instruction: Explain the specific thing asked, plainly, without teaching more than the question needs.

grades.name: Guided Walkthrough
grades.description: Step-by-step, each step following from the last.
grades.instruction: Walk through the idea step by step, checking each step follows from the last, with one concrete illustration.

grades.name: Deep Explanation
grades.description: The mechanism, the why, and the common trap.
grades.instruction: Explain both how it works and why it is built that way — the mechanism, the reasons behind it, and the misconception most people trip on.

grades.name: Full Teaching Pass
grades.description: Teach it completely, ending with the next questions.
grades.instruction: Teach it completely: build from what the reader knows, layer the mechanism and the why, contrast it with what it is not, and end with the questions a sharp learner would ask next.

goals: Explain how it works and why it is that way.
Build from what the reader already knows.
Surface the misconception most people trip on.

grades.name: Full Interview
grades.description: Interview in batches to 95% confidence, then confirm the brief.
grades.instruction: Before any work, interview me in small batches of clarifying questions until you are at least 95% confident in the goal, constraints, and success criteria — if the context above is thin or missing, gather it here — then restate the brief in one short paragraph and wait for my confirmation.

grades.name: 95% Confidence Check
grades.description: Ask clarifying questions until 95% confident, then proceed.
grades.instruction: Ask me clarifying questions until you have 95% confidence in the answer; if the context above is thin or missing, fill the gaps through your questions, then proceed.

grades.name: Blocking Questions Only
grades.description: Ask only what would change the work; assume the rest.
grades.instruction: Ask only the questions whose answers would change the work; state your working assumptions for everything else and proceed.

grades.name: Assume & Log
grades.description: Never stop to ask; log every assumption made.
grades.instruction: Do not stop to ask questions; proceed on your best judgment and keep a visible log of every assumption you made and how to correct the work if one is wrong.

goals: Close the gaps in the brief before work begins.
Reach stated confidence before committing effort.
Make missing context explicit instead of guessed.

grades.name: Plain Answer
grades.description: The direct answer first, in plain sentences.
grades.instruction: Give the direct answer first, in plain sentences, before any elaboration.

grades.name: Answer Card
grades.description: One tight, scannable block of essentials.
grades.instruction: Present the essentials as one tight, scannable block: the answer, the two or three facts behind it, and nothing else.

grades.name: Information Brief
grades.description: Key facts, their context, and their implications.
grades.instruction: Deliver a brief that covers the key facts, the context that makes them meaningful, and their implications.

grades.name: Reference Piece
grades.description: A reference others can rely on, with caveats and examples.
grades.instruction: Write it as a reference others can rely on: definitions where terms could be misread, caveats where the answer bends, and examples where abstraction hides the point.

goals: Answer the question directly.
Keep the important information easy to scan.
Add context only when it helps understanding.

grades.name: Loose Bullets
grades.description: A short bullet list for the main points.
grades.instruction: Carry the main points as a short bullet list.

grades.name: Grouped Points
grades.description: Related points grouped under plain labels.
grades.instruction: Group related points under short plain labels so the reader can jump to what matters.

grades.name: Sectioned Points
grades.description: The whole answer as labeled key-point sections.
grades.instruction: Organize the whole answer as labeled key-point sections, one idea per point.

grades.name: Checklist Discipline
grades.description: Atomic, checkable points that can be ticked off.
grades.instruction: Make every point atomic and checkable — one action or fact each — so the list can be worked through and ticked off.

goals: Make the response easy to skim.
Keep each point focused on one idea.
Help the reader find the useful part quickly.

grades.name: One-Liner
grades.description: Open with the single sentence that matters.
grades.instruction: Open with the single sentence a busy reader needs.

grades.name: Quick Summary
grades.description: A few sentences of summary before the detail.
grades.instruction: Open with a two-to-four sentence summary of the result before the detail.

grades.name: Executive Summary
grades.description: Findings, what they mean, and the recommended move.
grades.instruction: Open with an executive summary: the findings, what they mean, and the recommended move.

grades.name: Standalone Abstract
grades.description: An abstract that works for someone who reads nothing else.
grades.instruction: Open with an abstract that stands alone — conclusions, key caveats, and the decision it supports — for a reader who reads nothing else.

goals: Put the main conclusion where it is easy to find.
Surface the findings that change the decision.
Connect findings to implications or next steps.

grades.name: Natural Flow
grades.description: Headings only where they genuinely help.
grades.instruction: Let the answer flow naturally; add a heading only where it genuinely helps.

grades.name: Clear Sections
grades.description: Short, clearly headed sections with one job each.
grades.instruction: Break the answer into short, clearly headed sections with one job each.

grades.name: Set Sequence
grades.description: A defined section sequence, every section kept.
grades.instruction: Follow a defined section sequence and keep every section, even if only to say it is not applicable.

grades.name: Locked Template
grades.description: The requested structure exactly, nothing added or dropped.
grades.instruction: Match the requested structure exactly — section names, order, and fields — with no additions or omissions.

goals: Give each section one clear job.
Use an order the reader can follow quickly.
Match the requested structure when one is supplied.

grades.name: Source Notes
grades.description: Name the sources that did the most work.
grades.instruction: Name the sources that did the most work, informally.

grades.name: Linked Sources
grades.description: Cite supporting sources inline, with links.
grades.instruction: Cite supporting sources inline, with links where they exist.

grades.name: Evidence Notes
grades.description: Tie findings to evidence and the weight it bears.
grades.instruction: Tie each major finding to its evidence and note how much weight it can bear.

grades.name: Citation Record
grades.description: Every important claim cited; inference marked as such.
grades.instruction: Give every important factual claim a citation, mark which claims rest on inference instead, and list the sources at the end.

goals: Connect important claims to their sources.
Make confidence easy to inspect.
Distinguish supported fact from interpretation.

grades.name: Option Notes
grades.description: Alternatives clearly separated in prose.
grades.instruction: Keep the alternatives clearly separated in prose.

grades.name: Comparison Table
grades.description: A compact table against the criteria that matter.
grades.instruction: Put the alternatives in a compact table against the criteria that matter.

grades.name: Decision Table
grades.description: Explicit criteria; the winner defensible at a glance.
grades.instruction: Build the table around explicit decision criteria, and make the winner's row defensible at a glance.

grades.name: Evaluation Matrix
grades.description: Weights, scores, rationale, and a ranked verdict.
grades.instruction: Use a strict matrix — criteria, weights, scores, one-line rationale per cell — and finish with the ranked verdict.

goals: Place alternatives against the same criteria.
Make differences and tradeoffs easy to scan.
End with a clear judgment when one is requested.

grades.name: Next Move
grades.description: The single next action worth taking.
grades.instruction: End with the single next action worth taking.

grades.name: Next Steps
grades.description: A short ordered list of next steps.
grades.instruction: End with a short ordered list of next steps.

grades.name: Prioritized Actions
grades.description: Priorities with owners or timing where known.
grades.instruction: End with prioritized actions — each with an owner or timeframe where known.

grades.name: Execution Handoff
grades.description: A handoff someone could execute cold.
grades.instruction: End with a handoff someone could execute cold: actions, owners, dependencies, and how to verify each is done.

goals: End with the next useful action.
Order follow-up work by priority.
Include owners, timing, or dependencies when known.

grades.name: Tight Budget
grades.description: Under ~150 words; say what got cut.
grades.instruction: Keep the entire response under roughly 150 words; if it cannot fit, say what you cut.

grades.name: One Screen
grades.description: About one screen; density over coverage.
grades.instruction: Keep the response to about one screen — roughly 300 words — favoring density over coverage.

grades.name: Room to Explain
grades.description: The space the subject needs, spent on substance.
grades.instruction: Take the space the subject needs, but spend it on substance: no throat-clearing, no restating the question, no padded transitions.

grades.name: Complete Treatment
grades.description: As long as completeness demands and no longer.
grades.instruction: Be as long as completeness demands and no longer — every section must earn its length, and repetition or filler is a defect.

goals: Set an explicit length contract.
Spend words on substance, not ceremony.
Treat padding as a defect.

grades.name: Essentials First
grades.description: Lead with the must-know; add depth only as needed.
grades.instruction: Lead with the essentials a reader must know, then add depth only where it earns its place.

grades.name: Three Tiers
grades.description: Break it into three tiers: essentials, working detail, edge.
grades.instruction: Break the content into three tiers of information: the essentials everyone needs, the working detail for people acting on it, and the deep or edge material that completes the picture.

grades.name: Tiered Sections
grades.description: Three labeled tiers as sections; every item assigned.
grades.instruction: Organize the response as three labeled tiers — essentials, working detail, and deep material — and place every piece of information in exactly one tier.

grades.name: Locked Tier Hierarchy
grades.description: Strict tier discipline; nothing lives outside the hierarchy.
grades.instruction: Enforce a strict three-tier hierarchy: name each tier, state what belongs in it, keep every section inside its declared tier, and cut anything that fits no tier.

goals: Serve every reader the depth they need.
Separate essentials from supporting detail.
Keep deep material from burying the point.

grades.name: First Contact
grades.description: No prior knowledge assumed; first principles.
grades.instruction: Assume no prior knowledge: explain from first principles and use everyday words before introducing any term of art.

grades.name: Plain Language
grades.description: Smart-generalist language; define terms on first use.
grades.instruction: Write for a smart generalist: define specialized terms on first use and prefer the plain word when it exists.

grades.name: Working Vocabulary
grades.description: Standard terminology, clarified only when obscure.
grades.instruction: Use the field's standard terminology freely, clarifying only genuinely obscure terms.

grades.name: Expert Shorthand
grades.description: Full technical vocabulary for an expert peer.
grades.instruction: Write for an expert peer: full technical vocabulary, no introductory explanations, precision over accessibility.

goals: Match terminology to the reader's knowledge.
Explain unfamiliar terms at the right depth.
Avoid background the audience does not need.

grades.name: Straight Talk
grades.description: Natural, direct, conversational language.
grades.instruction: Write like a sharp colleague talking: contractions, natural rhythm, no stiffness.

grades.name: Clear Neutral
grades.description: Calm, neutral language without ceremony.
grades.instruction: Keep the language calm and neutral — no ceremony, no chattiness.

grades.name: Professional Voice
grades.description: Polished, precise workplace language.
grades.instruction: Use polished, precise professional language fit for a workplace document.

grades.name: Formal Register
grades.description: Disciplined formal phrasing throughout.
grades.instruction: Hold a disciplined formal register throughout: complete phrasing, exact wording, nothing colloquial.

goals: Match formality to the setting.
Keep the register consistent throughout.
Change the register without losing clarity.

grades.name: Everyday Analogy
grades.description: Familiar examples before the abstract version.
grades.instruction: Anchor each major idea with an everyday example or analogy before the abstract version.

grades.name: Worked Example
grades.description: One example taken start to finish.
grades.instruction: Include one worked example that goes start to finish, not just the setup.

grades.name: Domain Example
grades.description: Realistic examples with the messy details left in.
grades.instruction: Use realistic domain examples with the messy details left in, since that is where the lesson lives.

grades.name: Edge Case
grades.description: Examples that expose the boundaries of the rule.
grades.instruction: Choose examples that expose the boundaries — the edge case, the counterexample, the place the rule bends.

goals: Use examples that fit the reader's experience.
Make abstract ideas concrete.
Choose examples that expose the important detail.

grades.name: Next Decision
grades.description: What to decide next and what is needed to decide it.
grades.instruction: Make explicit what the reader should decide next and what they need in order to decide it.

grades.name: Actionable Framing
grades.description: Frame around the actions the answer enables.
grades.instruction: Frame the answer around the actions it enables: what to do, in what order, and what to watch for.

grades.name: Tradeoff Brief
grades.description: Center what is gained, given up, and which way to lean.
grades.instruction: Center the material tradeoffs — what is gained, what is given up, and which way the evidence leans.

grades.name: Decision Record
grades.description: Options, choice, rationale, and accepted consequences.
grades.instruction: Frame the answer as a decision record: the options considered, the choice, the rationale, and the consequences accepted.

goals: Show the choices the reader must make.
Explain consequences and tradeoffs.
Write at a level the reader can act on.

grades.name: Warm & Encouraging
grades.description: Acknowledge the difficulty; make the next step feel doable.
grades.instruction: Take a warm, encouraging stance: acknowledge the difficulty, and make the next step feel doable.

grades.name: Even & Matter-of-Fact
grades.description: State things as they are, without cheerleading or alarm.
grades.instruction: Keep an even, matter-of-fact stance: state things as they are, without cheerleading or alarm.

grades.name: Candid & Direct
grades.description: Lead with conclusions; say the uncomfortable part.
grades.instruction: Be candid: lead with conclusions, skip the hedging, and say the uncomfortable part out loud, professionally.

grades.name: Authoritative & Decisive
grades.description: Firm conclusions and unambiguous requirements.
grades.instruction: Take the authoritative stance of the accountable expert: firm conclusions, unambiguous requirements, and no false balance.

goals: Set how assertive and warm the answer should feel.
Say the uncomfortable part at the right volume.
Keep the stance consistent from open to close.
